import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

When you make a Papercusp lib reusable by any project — or notice domain
coupling leaking into one that's supposed to be generic — follow this
pattern. It's the one used across the 2026-05-31 generalization pass
(plan `papercusp-systems-abstraction-2026-05-29`, D-011).

## The pattern, in one line

> **The package names no project. The host injects domain values through a
> small seam (a `configure*()` call or a React prop). The operator maps its
> own domain onto that seam at the boundary** — so the live app stays
> byte-identical while the lib becomes borrowable.

Concretely, three shapes recur:

- **`configure*()` host seam** (server libs). The lib exposes
  `configureX({ ... })` and reads the injected values at runtime; the
  operator calls it once in a `lib/<x>/configure.ts` imported for side
  effect. Examples: `configureMemory({ schema, defaultDbName, localStoreDir })`,
  `configureDesktopIpc({ forceHttp })`, `configureBackup`, `configureLocks`.
- **Options on the entry function.** When there's a natural call site,
  add options instead of a global: `startEndpointIpcServer({ readyToken,
  socketPath, upstreamBaseUrl })`. The operator passes its branded values;
  the lib defaults to neutral ones.
- **React props + a config Context** (UI libs). Add props with neutral
  defaults; thread them to memo'd children via a small Context so you
  don't prop-drill. Example: LogView's `appLinks` / `primarySource` /
  `bookmarkKeyPrefix`.

The operator keeps the brand. e.g. `@papercusp/ipc-endpoint-server` emits
a generic `IPC_READY` handshake by default; the operator injects
`readyToken: 'PAPERCUSP_IPC_READY'` to satisfy the papercusp-desktop Rust
client. The lib names nothing; the host owns the wiring.

## The soft-coupling checklist (what to hunt for)

Compile-time imports of domain packages (`@papercusp/db-org|harness|
orchestrator|agent-mcp|zero-harness|papercusp-shared`) are the obvious
coupling and usually already gone. The **soft** coupling is what hides:

1. **Hardcoded PG schema / db names** in SQL — `harness_shared.*`,
   default db `papercusp`. → inject a `schema` / `defaultDbName`.
2. **Filesystem paths** — `~/.papercusp`, `.papercusp/`, `apps/operator/...`.
   → inject a dir, default to `os.tmpdir()`.
3. **Branded env-var names** — `PAPERCUSP_*`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAPERCUSP_*`.
   → a `configure()` field, or a generic-named env fallback.
4. **Branded global / window keys** — `__restart*__`, `__papercusp*__`.
   Make them fully neutral (`__sse_channel_registry__`), not just
   renamed to your own scope. "Self-namespaced by the package" still
   reads as coupling — go neutral.
5. **Domain vocab in a PUBLIC type/field** — `harnessSlug`, `harness_slug`,
   `feature_id`. → rename to neutral (`scope`, `scopeFilter`); the
   operator maps its column onto it and maps back in its output.
6. **Generated-output banners / strings.** A tokens/codegen lib that
   prepends `AUTO-GENERATED by @papercusp/...` brands *the consumer's*
   files. → neutral default + an override option.

<Aside type="caution" title="grep is not enough">
Items 4 and 6 are routinely missed by a string grep over imports/paths —
a global key looks like any identifier, and a banner is a generated
string, not an import. **Read the source.** The 2026-05-31 deep audit
(four parallel Explore agents reading source, not grepping) caught the
`token-kit` banner, the `sse`/`sync` global keys, and confirmed the rest
clean — after a grep-level pass had marked them "clean".
</Aside>

## Verify the host still behaves identically

For each generalized lib: run its own test suite + a typecheck, and run
the **one operator test that exercises the seam end-to-end** if it exists
(e.g. `dev_ipc_echo_e2e.test.ts` confirmed the operator still emits the
real `PAPERCUSP_IPC_READY` handshake through the new `readyToken` option).
The `npm run test:affected` walker is **not** a usable gate in a bare
sandbox — the operator's integration suite needs Docker/embedded-PG and
mass-times-out without it. Verify per-lib instead.

## What stays coupled — and why that's correct

Not everything should be generalized. Keep the tie-in when the lib *is*
the domain contract: the plugin SDK/loader (`PapercuspContext`, the
`papercusp.json` manifest), the flag registry (the keys *are* the
product), `host-platform` (the designated host layer). Generalizing those
would just recreate a generic shell with none of the value (plan D-008).
Some seam'd libs (`locks`, `coordination`, `backup`, `docs-engine`) keep
a Papercusp tie-in by decision even though they have a host seam.

## Discoverability + grouping tooling

- **Catalog:** `BORROWABLE.md` at the repo root, generated by
  `scripts/gen-borrowable-catalog.mjs` (`npm run gen:borrowable`, and
  `:check` as a CI staleness guard). Membership is curated in the script
  (not a package.json keyword) so adding a submodule never needs a
  submodule commit. When you make a lib generic, add it there.
- **Physical grouping** under `libs/generic/`:
  `scripts/regroup-borrowable-libs.sh` does the atomic move (git mv each
  submodule + repoint every `node_modules/@papercusp/*` symlink + rewrite
  workspace globs + regen the catalog). It is **safe because consumers
  import by package name, not path**. It self-aborts unless the operator
  is stopped and every target submodule is clean. **Executed 2026-05-31**
  (plan D-012) — the 9 borrowable submodules now live at `libs/generic/`.

<Aside type="danger" title="A path move is more than symlinks — three gotchas (D-012)">
Repointing `node_modules/@papercusp/*` symlinks makes the *running*
operator resolve fine, but it is **not** the whole job:

1. **Path refs beyond symlinks go stale.** Repointing symlinks + the root
   workspace globs is not enough — a path move must also rewrite: `file:`
   workspace deps (`apps/operator/package.json`, `packages/agent-mcp/package.json`
   declare `"@papercusp/x": "file:../../libs/x"` — breaks a fresh `npm install`),
   `.github/workflows` working-dirs, `scripts/scaffold-tests.mjs` dirs, docs
   `--workspace` paths, **`Dockerfile` `COPY` lines**, and **test-discovery
   globs** (`packages/operator-core/lib/testing-domains-registry.ts`). Grep every file
   type, not just `*.json`/`*.yml`. (Skip refs that are example harness sub-slugs
   like `papercup/libs/sync`, and `Dockerfile.papercup` — bannered "do not fix".)
2. **The operator services are transient `systemd-run --user` units**
   (`papercup-dev-api` = :3070 host, CWD `apps/operator`; `papercup-dev` =
   operator-vite watcher, CWD repo root). `systemctl --user stop` **destroys**
   a transient unit — you can't `start` it back. Recreate with
   `systemd-run --user --unit=<name> --working-directory=<dir>
   --property=Restart=always /usr/bin/bash -c '<exec>'`.
3. **Shared-index commit hazard:** `git commit` commits the whole index — in
   this multi-agent checkout another session may have left files staged.
   **Always `git diff --cached --name-only` before committing.**
</Aside>

## Going-forward: start generic-first (the lint)

Migrating a batch of misfiled cores out of the app is a one-time cleanup; the
*recurring* failure is writing the next generic core inside the app again. The
2026-06-05 audit (`generalize-libs-to-generic-2026-06-05`, D-005) added a guard so
the debt doesn't re-accrue:

- **`npm run lint:generic-first`** (advisory; `:all` for a full-tree sweep,
  `--strict` to exit non-zero) — `scripts/check-generic-first.mjs`. It flags a
  *substantial* file in `operator-core/lib` / `apps/operator/lib` that **both**
  (a) has zero papercusp coupling (no relative import, no domain `@papercusp/*`, no
  DB/IO client) **and** (b) *names* a textbook CS concept (supervision tree, fencing
  token, topological sort, token bucket, φ-accrual, saga…). It nudges the file toward
  `libs/generic/<name>` behind a seam.
- **Both signals are required on purpose.** Structural decoupling alone flags ~200
  files (most app code imports little); the concept name is the precision filter that
  separates a real misfiled algorithm from ordinary decoupled glue. The tradeoff is
  that a generic algorithm with an unlisted name is a false negative — acceptable for
  an advisory lint; a 200-candidate cry-wolf is not. Extend `CONCEPT_RE` when a new
  concept family recurs.
- **Default mode is diff-scoped** (mirrors `affected-tests.mjs`: added/modified `.ts`
  since the merge-base with `origin/main`, plus working-tree edits) so it nudges at the
  point of introduction in a PR. `--all` audits the whole tree.
- A genuinely app-local file whose concept keyword is incidental (e.g. ElevenLabs MSE
  "backpressure" = browser audio buffering) goes in the `ALLOW` set in the script — not
  a blanket suppression.

Informational by default (like `lint:knip` — never gates a merge). The convention it
guards is the "Borrowable libraries" section of the repo `CLAUDE.md` + `BORROWABLE.md`.
